description: Top-level folders named after technical kinds (`components/`, `hooks/`, `services/`). Simple at first; scatters each feature across the tree as the app grows.
Top-level folders named after domain areas (`features/cart`, `features/catalog`), each holding its own components, hooks and API calls.
Robert C. Martin's idea that the folder structure should announce the business domain, not the framework.
A reference React project: feature folders, no cross-feature imports, unidirectional `shared → features → app` flow enforced by ESLint.
Keep code next to where it is used; promote it outward only when a second real consumer appears.
Domain-free building blocks: UI primitives, generic hooks, the API client, formatting, config. Never imports features.
